name: Nobu Las Vegas at Caesars Palace
positioning: Nobu Hotel at Caesars Palace: the world's first Nobu Hotel, a Japanese-inspired hotel in its own tower at Caesars Palace on the center Strip
best_for: Travelers who want a calmer, Japanese-inspired hotel within Caesars Palace
Suite guests who value extras like Porsche house car rides and butler service

facts.text: Nobu Hotel occupies a separate tower at Caesars Palace, in the center of the Las Vegas Strip.
The hotel is decorated with zen plum and gold accent furnishings and artwork.
Nobu's nature theme is reminiscent of a quiet Japanese garden.
Partial Strip View rooms are on the upper floors of Nobu Hotel.
The Nobu Penthouse has a curved staircase with a second-story terrace and a stone hearth wall.
Butler service is included in all Penthouse and Villa bookings.
Nobu Penthouse and Villa guests receive complimentary airport transfers in a luxury Escalade.
Guests have the exclusive Nobu Pool plus access to all seven Caesars Palace pools.
Qua Spa at Caesars Palace has three Roman baths and a snowing Arctic Ice Room.
Nobu Hotel has its own private fitness area for guests.
Nobu Hotel guests receive dedicated concierge service and priority seating at Nobu Restaurant.

highlights.text: Nobu Hotel at Caesars Palace is the world's first Nobu Hotel.
The Nobu Villa is a Japanese-inspired rooftop villa with a large patio overlooking the Strip and a secluded Zen garden with an Italian-made whirlpool.
The decor of the Nobu Deluxe rooms is inspired by kintsugi, the Japanese art of repairing broken pottery with gold epoxy.
The Tanoshi Wellness Hour is a nightly rotation of calming rituals, from sound bowls to tea moments, in the Nobu Hotel Living Room.
Nobu Hotel suite guests get complimentary rides within a 10-mile radius in the hotel's Porsche house cars, subject to availability.

considerations.text: Nobu Hotel sits within Caesars Palace, with the sprawling casino only steps away from the rooms.
The Porsche house cars carry up to three guests and cannot take large luggage.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's luxury positioning.
